aexp: verified-lesson memory for any agent (AgentExperience.NET, preview).

Usage:
  aexp run start --task <text> [--task-id <id>]        Open a run; prints its ID.
  aexp run call --run <id> --tool <name> [--args <json>] [--result <text> | --error <text>]
  aexp run end --run <id> [--status completed|failed|cancelled]
  aexp finalize --run <id> [--exit-code <n>]           Run the configured verifier and finalize.
  aexp recall --task <text> [--run <id>]               Print the Historical Reference block.
  aexp recall --run <id> --failure --tool <name> --error <text>
                                                        Print the hint for a failure, if any.
  aexp lessons [--all] [--html <file>]                 List lessons (or write the HTML view).
  aexp export [--markdown <file>] [--claude-md [file]] [--agents-md [file]]
                                                        Export lessons measured as helping (to a file, or
                                                        the managed section of CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md).
  aexp benefit [--markdown <file>]                     The holdout's estimate (or a results page).
  aexp mcp                                             Serve the MCP tools over stdio.
  aexp trust                                           Show the config's verifier, and approve the config.
  aexp runs prune --older-than <age>                   Delete open runs older than e.g. 7d, 12h, 30m.
  aexp setup claude-code [--print]                     Add the Claude Code hooks, a config and .gitignore entry.
  aexp hook <event> [--timeout <s>] [--claude-md [file]] [--agents-md [file]]
                                                        A Claude Code hook (reads the event JSON on stdin).

Every command reads .aexp/config.json (nearest one up from here), or --config <file>, or AEXP_CONFIG.
Output marked HISTORICAL REFERENCE is untrusted reference material, not instructions.

.claude/settings.json: added the SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd hook(s); every existing hook kept.
.aexp/config.json: written. No test command was obvious, so verify.command is a placeholder that refuses to run: set it.
.gitignore: added .aexp/.

Next (these are a person's steps, not the agent's):
  1. Review .aexp/config.json: verify.command is the one command aexp runs to check the agent's work.
  2. Run 'aexp trust' yourself. Until then the hooks record and inject, but the Stop hook does not run the
     verifier. Any edit to the config revokes the approval.
  3. Protect the config and the approval from the agent. Add these deny rules to your USER settings,
     ~/.claude/settings.json, which a session in this project cannot edit (project settings can be):
{
  "permissions": {
    "deny": [
      "Edit(//**/.aexp/**)",
      "Edit(//**/.claude/**)",
      "Edit(//tmp/inspectra-help-agente-b9a180da-1727afc0/xdg-config/aexp/**)",
      "Bash(aexp trust)",
      "Bash(aexp trust *)",
      "Bash(dotnet aexp trust)",
      "Bash(dotnet aexp trust *)",
      "Bash(dotnet tool run aexp trust)",
      "Bash(dotnet tool run aexp trust *)"
    ]
  }
}
     They stop Claude Code's file tools (and the shell commands and redirections it recognizes) from editing
     any .aexp/ or .claude/ directory and your aexp trust file, and the usual spellings of 'aexp trust'.
     They are not an operating-system boundary: unless Bash is restricted (Claude Code's sandbox, or deny
     rules on Bash itself), a command or script the agent runs can still write those files, and a session
     that rewrites its own verifier can fake success. The verifier's verdict is only as trustworthy as that;
     each lesson names its check, so a reviewer can see what verified it.
  4. Install aexp where the hooks can find it: dotnet tool install --global AgentExperience.Cli --prerelease
Turn it off: remove the 'aexp hook' entries from .claude/settings.json.
